author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be corrected afterwards. The correction is offered prefilled with the visit's stored date and description, is held to the same rules as booking, and updates the existing visit rather than adding a second one to the pet.
acceptance_criteria: Given an existing visit, when it is opened for correction, then the same form used for booking is shown carrying that visit's stored date and description.
Given an existing visit, when a description and a date later than today are supplied, then that visit carries the new date and description and the owner's record is shown.
Given an existing visit, when a correction is accepted, then the pet holds the same number of visits as before.
Given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then the correction is refused, the description is named, and the form is shown again.
Given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then the correction is refused, the date is named, and the form is shown again.
Given a visit that does not belong to the named pet, or a pet that does not belong to the named owner, when a correction is attempted, then it is refused.
non_goals: Cancelling or deleting a booked visit — NG-5 keeps cancellation out and NG-4 keeps deletion out
Correcting a visit whose date has already passed — the future-date rule applies to a correction, so a past visit is not correctable (Visits edge case 4, and an open question)
A way to reach the correction from the owner's record — REQ-VIS-003 states what a correction does, not where a reader starts one
notes: NG-5 narrowed 2026-08-04 by product-owner decision; recorded in docs/prd.md Non-Goals and docs/adr/2026-08-04-non-goal-visit-correction.md. Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records in the log, skipped. Out of my write scope and left undone: the new ADR needs an index row in docs/adr/README.md. Two open questions recorded in docs/prd.md, neither blocking this slice: whether a past visit should be correctable, and how a correction is reached.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The correction reuses the create-or-update controller shape PetController already demonstrates, inside the existing owner feature package. No new module, no new type, no service layer, no new dependency. The single adjustment is to VisitController's @ModelAttribute("visit") loader: it currently constructs a fresh Visit and calls pet.addVisit(visit) unconditionally, and it runs before every handler in the controller. Make it visitId-aware exactly as PetController.findPet is petId-aware (@PathVariable(name = "visitId", required = false) Integer visitId) — absent visitId keeps today's new-visit branch; present visitId returns the stored Visit reached by traversal and adds nothing. That branch is the whole in-place constraint: nothing is added, so nothing can duplicate. Aggregate traversal stays as system-design.md Contracts § Invariants the rows cannot carry records it — Owner is the entry point, Pet is reached through Owner, Visit through Pet, and OwnerRepository remains the sole write path.
integration_points: GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit added to VisitController, mapped to the existing pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm view
Pet gains a getVisit(Integer id) traversal accessor mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer id), including its skip-unsaved guard
VisitController.loadPetWithVisit gains the nullable visitId branch and is shared by the booking and correction routes
No change to OwnerRepository, Visit, Owner, or the persistence schema

patterns.description: The create-or-update pattern to copy: a nullable-id @ModelAttribute loader, an initUpdateForm GET that only names the view, a processUpdateForm POST that revalidates and redirects to redirect:/owners/{ownerId}, and an @InitBinder disallowing id binding. Mirror the method naming (initUpdateVisitForm / processUpdateVisitForm).

Owner.getPet(Integer id) is the traversal accessor to mirror for Pet.getVisit(Integer id): iterate the owned collection, skip unsaved members, compare with Objects.equals, return null when absent. Keeping the lookup in the model rather than a controller stream keeps traversal in the aggregate.

How the update persists in place: loadPetWithVisit loads the Owner once and puts owner and pet into the model, so the handler's @ModelAttribute Owner owner resolves that same model instance rather than issuing a second findById. The Visit the loader returns is therefore the live member of pet.getVisits() inside that graph, MVC binds the submitted date and description straight onto it, and this.owners.save(owner) cascades a merge that updates the existing row by id. The correction handler must NOT call owner.addVisit(petId, visit) and must NOT copy fields onto a second instance — either would re-enter the create path. This differs from PetController.updatePetDetails, which copies precisely because findOwner and findPet there issue two separate findById calls and so hold two distinct graphs; VisitController does not have that problem.

risks.risk: The in-place update is implicit — a reader sees a POST handler that validates and calls save() with no visible mutation, because the mutation happened during binding. A later maintainer may 'fix' it by adding an addVisit call and silently reintroduce the duplicate.
risks.mitigation: Name the branch in loadPetWithVisit so the two cases are visible at the loader, and keep the prd-entry's theVisitCorrectionShouldLeaveThePetsVisitCountUnchanged test as the executable guard on the constraint.

risks.risk: A new user-facing label on the correction form (for example an 'Update Visit' button or heading) would need a message key in all eleven bundles under src/main/resources/messages/. I18nPropertiesSyncTest enforces key parity across bundles and also scans templates for non-internationalized strings, so a partial addition fails the build — this is REQ-LANG-002's enforcement.
risks.mitigation: Change no template text. The form already carries no action attribute, so it posts to whichever URL rendered it and serves both routes unchanged; verify that by test rather than by editing the template. If a flash message is wanted on success, follow the existing literal-string convention in the sibling handlers rather than introducing a key.

risks.risk: Identifier tampering — a visitId belonging to another pet, or a petId belonging to another owner.
risks.mitigation: Already closed by the design rather than by an added check: there is no VisitRepository and no global lookup by visit id, so the only way to the Visit is owner -> pet -> visit. A foreign id simply is not found. Refuse it the way the loader already refuses a missing pet — an IllegalArgumentException from the loader — and keep the @InitBinder id and *.id disallow so identity comes from the path and never from the form. This covers PRD Visits edge case 3.

risks.risk: The non-future-date rule is currently inline in processNewVisitForm and would be duplicated by the correction handler.
risks.mitigation: Extract it to one private method in VisitController called from both handlers, keeping the rejectValue code typeMismatch.visitDate identical so the existing message key and the new tests agree.

notes: Basis for the covered-by-existing-pattern claim: direct reads of PetController, Owner, Pet, Visit, VisitController and the form template, not a text match; no IDE oracle is connected in this dispatch, so no search_symbol citation accompanies it. Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log, skipped. Wrote docs/adr/README.md — index row added for docs/adr/2026-08-04-non-goal-visit-correction.md as requested; that ADR is a product non-goal decision already recorded, and no new ADR is warranted for this slice, whose choices are local and reversible. docs/system-design.md is deliberately NOT updated ahead of the code: it carries current state only. Once the slice lands, three Contracts rows need me, not doc-sync — VisitController's purpose text and Implements, and the Implements column on Pet and Visit, all gaining REQ-VIS-003. Presentation consequence worth knowing before it is mistaken for a defect: the template's Previous Visits table filters on the iterated visit being unsaved, which is what hides the placeholder Visit the booking loader adds; on the correction form every visit is saved, so the visit under correction appears in its own Previous Visits list. Nothing in REQ-VIS-002 or REQ-VIS-003 speaks to that, so it is out of scope here. Test note: VisitControllerTests stubs OwnerRepository.findById to return one Owner instance, so the correction tests can seed a Visit with an id into that pet and then assert the new date, the new description, and the unchanged visit count directly on the in-memory aggregate after the POST — no Mockito verify needed, which suits the project's minimal-mocking stance.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: loadPetWithVisit now carries three responsibilities at once: resolve the owner, resolve the pet, and — new in this slice — decide which Visit the form binds to (a fresh unsaved Visit vs. the pet's own stored Visit). The nullable-visitId branch itself is the right call and mirrors an established codebase idiom (PetController.findPet is petId-aware the same way across /pets/new and /pets/{petId}/edit), so the loader's contract is not wrong, but the load-bearing invariant — that a correction adds nothing to the pet — now lives only in the method's Javadoc prose and in the processUpdateVisitForm comment, not in a named unit of code a reader can jump to. Pulling the visitId branch into a small private helper (e.g. `private Visit resolveVisit(Pet pet, Integer visitId, int petId)`, returning a new unsaved Visit when visitId is null and the stored Visit — or throwing — otherwise) would let loadPetWithVisit read as 'find owner, find pet, resolveVisit', giving the invariant a name instead of only a comment.
findings.fix: Extract the `if (visitId == null) { ... } ... return storedVisit;` block (lines 84-95) into a private `resolveVisit(Pet pet, Integer visitId, int petId)` helper and have loadPetWithVisit call it after populating the model. No behavior change; purely a readability extraction.

approved_aspects:
The nullable @PathVariable(name = "visitId", required = false) branch in the controller-wide @ModelAttribute loader is the clearest expression of the in-place-correction constraint available in this codebase: it mirrors the pre-existing PetController.findPet pattern exactly (verified by reading PetController.java:75-84), it is documented in the loader's Javadoc (the visitId param and the added

paragraph), and it is guarded by an executable test (theVisitCorrectionShouldLeaveThePetsVisitCountUnchanged). Splitting owner/pet lookup from visit resolution into a second @ModelAttribute method would need to repeat or reorder the traversal already done here, which is a worse alternative than the one autofix suggestion above.

Pet.getVisit(Integer id) mirrors Owner.getPet(Integer id) field-for-field (skip-unsaved guard, Objects.equals comparison, same null-return contract) — a deliberate, well-placed consistency choice for a traversal accessor.
rejectDateNotInFuture is a clean single-responsibility extraction shared correctly by both handlers, preserving the existing rejectValue error code so no test or message key needed to change.
processUpdateVisitForm's comment correctly states why it must not call addVisit, guarding against the exact regression the design-block's risk section named.
./gradlew checkFormat: BUILD SUCCESSFUL, no formatting issues in the changed files.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: docs/prd.md's Visits edge-case table lists edge case 3 as two clauses: 'Correcting a visit that does not belong to the named pet is refused, as is correcting one whose pet does not belong to the named owner.' The suite covers only the first clause (theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitBelongsToAnotherPet, using VISIT_ID_OF_ANOTHER_PET). No test drives the correction routes with a petId that does not belong to TEST_OWNER_ID, so the loader's 'Pet with id ... not found for owner with id ...' branch is untested by this slice. This mirrors a pre-existing gap on the booking side (processNewVisitFormSuccess et al. never exercise a foreign petId either, and PetControllerTests has the same gap for PetController.findPet), so the defect is not newly introduced, but REQ-VIS-003's own prd-entry test_names omit it too and the PRD calls the case out by number for this requirement specifically.
findings.fix: Add theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenThePetBelongsToAnotherOwner: stub owners.findById for a second owner ID that does not own TEST_PET_ID (or reuse the existing owner but post to a petId the test never added to it), assert the same assertThatThrownBy(...).hasRootCauseInstanceOf(IllegalArgumentException.class) plus containsExactly(this.bookedVisit) on the untouched pet, matching the sibling test's shape.

approved_aspects: The load-bearing assertThat(this.pet.getVisits()).containsExactly(this.bookedVisit) in theVisitCorrectionShouldLeaveThePetsVisitCountUnchanged is a genuine regression guard, not a tautology: traced against VisitController, a regression that reintroduced the create path (either processUpdateVisitForm calling owner.addVisit(petId, visit) on the already-bound bookedVisit, or loadPetWithVisit reverting to always constructing a new Visit) would leave the pet holding two visits, failing containsExactly's single-element expectation. theVisitCorrectionShouldUpdateTheVisitInPlace's direct field assertions on this.bookedVisit independently catch the same regression class from the other direction (the stored visit's fields would stay at BOOKED_DATE/BOOKED_DESCRIPTION instead of moving to the corrected values).

theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitBelongsToAnotherPet correctly covers PRD edge case 3's first clause, using assertThatThrownBy(...).hasRootCauseInstanceOf(IllegalArgumentException.class) to unwrap MockMvc's ServletException wrapping, and additionally asserts the pet's visit list is untouched by the rejected attempt.

Redisplay-on-validation-failure is covered for both PRD edge cases (blank description, non-future date), each asserting the specific field error code and that the same view is redisplayed with status 200 rather than a redirect.

Fixture factories createOwnerWithPet()/createBookedVisit() and named constants (BOOKED_DATE, CORRECTED_DATE, CORRECTED_DESCRIPTION, NOT_FUTURE_DATE, BLANK_DESCRIPTION, VISIT_ID_OF_ANOTHER_PET) leave zero Tier-3 mystery literals in the six new tests and follow the BDD the{Subject}Should{Outcome} naming school for tests written after 2026-07-31.
Tests are independent: @BeforeEach rebuilds owner/pet/visit fresh per test, no shared mutable fixture across tests.

OwnerRepository stubbing via @MockitoBean is the pre-existing, tolerated mock-framework usage the brief permits (mock-framework stubs on existing collaborators are tolerated, not encouraged); MockMvc is the one sanctioned mock and is used correctly to drive real MVC binding/validation.
All 10 VisitControllerTests pass under ./gradlew test.

author: security-reviewer

findings.location: src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/VisitController.java:146 (processUpdateVisitForm, @ModelAttribute Owner owner) and docs/system-design.md Threat Model
findings.description: Non-blocking, no fix requested this pass — a documentation question about a surface the new endpoint replicates. The correction POST declares `@ModelAttribute Owner owner`, which Spring resolves from the model instance loadPetWithVisit put there and then RE-BINDS request parameters onto before the handler runs (ModelAttributeMethodProcessor calls bindRequestParameters on a model-sourced attribute unless binding=false). `this.owners.save(owner)` then cascades (CascadeType.ALL on Owner.pets and Pet.visits). The @InitBinder disallow covers `id` and `*.id`, so identity is safe, but every other field of the aggregate is bindable from the request body: a crafted POST to the correction URL carrying `telephone=abc`, `pets[0].name=...`, or `pets[0].visits[1].description=...` mutates and persists fields the correction form never offers, and because the Owner parameter is not annotated @Valid, it also bypasses Owner's @NotBlank/@Pattern bean validation (Threat Model row 'Unvalidated input reaching persistence' claims those constraints cover the form fields). Incremental risk this slice: none — /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/new carries the identical `@ModelAttribute Owner owner` + save(owner) shape today, and the whole application is unauthenticated by design (Security Context; Threat Model row 1 'Unauthenticated data modification', mitigation 'None observed'), so an attacker gains no capability the baseline does not already grant. That is why this is approved rather than blocked. It is raised because the change adds a second endpoint carrying the class and because security-principles.md warns that a demonstration pattern propagates further than the same pattern in a private product. Question for the design owner: record the aggregate-wide rebinding as an accepted invariant next to the new traversal invariant in system-design.md Contracts, or narrow it (`@ModelAttribute(binding = false) Owner owner` on both visit handlers — the handlers only need the loaded graph to save, never bound form data). Class sweep: processUpdateVisitForm is the only new binding path in this change set; the two GET handlers take no bound arguments, and Pet.getVisit performs no binding.

approved_aspects: TRAVERSAL CLAIM VERIFIED — the design's assertion that traversal, not an explicit authorization check, refuses a foreign identifier holds on both axes. Foreign visitId: loadPetWithVisit reaches the Visit only via pet.getVisit(visitId) (Pet.java:267-277), which iterates `this.visits` — the pet's own @OneToMany collection — and returns null for anything outside it; the loader then throws IllegalArgumentException (VisitController.java:90-94). Foreign petId: owner.getPet(petId) (Owner.java:117-127) iterates the owner's own `pets` list, loaded by findById(ownerId) from the path, and the null branch throws (VisitController.java:76-80). There is no escape hatch: `grep -rn 'VisitRepository|Visit>' src/main` confirms no VisitRepository and no global lookup by visit id exists — the only Visit references in production code are Pet's own collection and its accessor. An attacker mixing identifiers (owner A's ownerId with owner B's petId, or the right pet with another pet's visitId) reaches a null and an exception before any binding or persistence, and never a foreign object. Executable guard: theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitBelongsToAnotherPet asserts both the throw and that the pet's visit list is untouched.

MASS-ASSIGNMENT PROTECTION HOLDS ON THE NEW PATH — the @InitBinder setAllowedFields(dataBinder.setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id"), VisitController.java:51-54) is controller-scoped and unannotated by path, so it applies to every WebDataBinder the two new handlers create, exactly as it does to the pre-existing booking handlers. No new @InitBinder was added and none was narrowed. Visit identity therefore comes solely from the @PathVariable visitId consumed by the loader before binding; a submitted `id` or `visit.id` parameter is dropped, so an attacker cannot repoint the bound Visit at another row, and the in-place update targets the row the URL named. This satisfies security-principles.md § Realization row 'Mass assignment' (every request-bound type explicitly disallows identifier binding) and Threat Model row 'Mass assignment / identifier tampering via form binding'.

NO CROSS-REQUEST TRUST — processUpdateVisitForm does not trust that an earlier GET validated the identifiers. loadPetWithVisit runs as a controller-wide @ModelAttribute before every handler in the class, so the owner, pet, and visit are re-resolved and re-checked on the POST itself. Satisfies security-principles.md row 'Trusting cross-request state'.

NO INJECTION SURFACE ADDED — persistence stays on Spring Data JPA's derived findById plus the cascading save; no query text is built anywhere in the change, and no request-derived value composes a filesystem or classpath path. Satisfies the 'Injection into data access' and 'Path traversal' rows.

NO XSS INTRODUCED — the change touches no template. pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.html (now serving both routes) renders every request-derived value through th:text (pet.name, visit.description, owner names); `grep -rn 'utext' src/main/resources/templates/` returns nothing, so Thymeleaf's default escaping is intact and nothing disables it.

ERROR MESSAGES CARRY NO SENSITIVE VALUE — the new IllegalArgumentException text interpolates only the visitId and petId from the URL the caller already supplied. No credential, connection string, session identifier, or PII reaches it, so surfacing it on the error page (the known REQ-SYS-002 defect) leaks nothing new. Satisfies the 'Secret disclosure through logs and errors' row.

NO SECRETS IN THE DIFF — swept the change set for credential-shaped additions (token, password, secret, key, credential, passwd, pwd, api, auth, conn/jdbc strings). The only literals added are the flash message "Your visit has been updated", the view name, the error-code string typeMismatch.visitDate, and test fixture data (dates, descriptions, integer ids). No new credential of any kind.

SUPPLY CHAIN UNCHANGED — `git status --porcelain -- build.gradle pom.xml gradle/ settings.gradle` is empty and the change set (scripts/changeset.sh --name-only) contains no build or dependency file. No dependency was added, upgraded, or repointed, so the four checks in system-design.md § Adding a New Dependency are not triggered and no new CVE surface enters with this slice; the framework versions under review are the ones already in the baseline.

EXPOSED SURFACE STATED — the two new routes are declared in docs/prd.md (REQ-VIS-003 with its done-when list and edge case 3) and in system-design.md's VisitController contract row, and the traversal property is now recorded as an explicit invariant in § Contracts. Neither route is a management/actuator endpoint and neither broadens actuator exposure, so the 'Widening the exposed surface' row is satisfied.

findings.description: The amended Non-Goals provenance note keeps its unqualified claim 'That reason genuinely explains each row' (the demonstration-framing/breadth reason) and only appends a trailing exception sentence about NG-5 being 'decided rather than derived.' But NG-5's own rationale text no longer invokes the framing reason at all — it now reads 'Cancellation is deletion of a visit, which NG-4 already declines,' a different, NG-4-alignment reason. The note is therefore not fully accurate as amended: it still asserts the one framing reason explains every row, including NG-5, while NG-5's row demonstrably states a different reason. findings.description: Three sentences in the new ADR exceed the 30-word cap (Writing Standards), same class as the PRD instances: the Context sentence beginning 'The row was derived from the absence of both in the code...' (50 words), the Context sentence beginning 'A correction demonstrates the update half of a create-and-update flow...' findings.description: Two lines changed in this slice exceed the 30-word cap: the new clause in 'Invariants the rows cannot carry' ('A pet or a visit is therefore reached only by traversal from the owner named in the path, so an identifier belonging to another owner's graph is not found rather than being found and then rejected.' — 36 words) and the VisitController Contracts row's Purpose cell (34 words).

findings.description: The new Invariants clause states the traversal guard only at the owner level: 'an identifier belonging to another owner's graph is not found.' The actual mechanism, and the edge case it documents, is narrower and independent at a second level: Pet.getVisit(visitId) scopes to that pet's own visits collection, so a visitId belonging to a different pet under the SAME owner is refused by the identical traversal-miss mechanism, not just a visitId belonging to a different owner. This is exactly PRD Visits edge case 3's first clause ('Correcting a visit that does not belong to the named pet is refused') and the executable guard theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitBelongsToAnotherPet, neither of which requires the foreign pet to belong to another owner. As phrased, a reader would conclude the invariant only catches cross-owner tampering, understating what traversal actually guarantees.
findings.fix: State both traversal levels explicitly, e.g.: '...so a petId not among the named owner's own pets, or a visitId not among the resolved pet's own visits, is not found rather than being found and then rejected.'

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be corrected afterwards. The correction is offered prefilled with the visit's stored date and description, is held to the same rules as booking, and updates the existing visit rather than adding a second one to the pet.
acceptance_criteria: Given an existing visit, when it is opened for correction, then the same form used for booking is shown carrying that visit's stored date and description.
Given an existing visit, when a description and a date later than today are supplied, then that visit carries them and the owner's record is shown.
Given an existing visit, when a correction is accepted, then the pet holds the same number of visits as before.
Given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then the correction is refused, the description is named, and the form is shown again.
Given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then the correction is refused, the date is named, and the form is shown again.
Given a visit that does not belong to the named pet, or a pet that does not belong to the named owner, when a correction is attempted, then it is refused.
non_goals: Cancelling or deleting a booked visit — NG-5 keeps cancellation out and NG-4 keeps deletion out
Correcting a visit whose date has already passed — the future-date rule applies to a correction, so a past visit is not correctable (Visits edge case 4, and an open question)
A way to reach the correction from the owner's record — REQ-VIS-003 states what a correction does, not where a reader starts one
notes: Supersedes the prd-entry at line 2; no scope change. Processes the two doc-reviewer blocked findings on docs/prd.md from the review-feedback at line 19. (1) 30-word cap, docs/prd.md:105,113: the Visits narrative sentence was split in two, and the second REQ-VIS-003 'Done when' bullet was trimmed from 31 to 27 words by replacing 'carries the new date and description' with 'carries them' — the given/when/then content is unchanged. Acceptance criterion 2 above is reworded to match the trimmed bullet, same meaning. No sentence in docs/prd.md now exceeds 30 words. (2) Provenance note, docs/prd.md:35: the framing-reason claim is scoped to exclude NG-5 ('every row but NG-5'), the lead sentence now reads 'covers all but one row', and the trailing sentence states NG-5's actual basis — it rests on NG-4, not on the framing reason — so the note and the NG-5 rationale cell agree. Out of scope this round: the 30-word-cap finding on docs/adr/2026-08-04-non-goal-visit-correction.md, which routes to system-design-expert. Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records in the log, skipped. The two open questions (whether a past visit should be correctable, and how a correction is reached) remain recorded as open and unresolved; neither blocks this slice.

The single adjustment was making VisitController's @ModelAttribute("visit") loader visitId-aware exactly as PetController.findPet is petId-aware — absent visitId keeps the new-visit branch, present visitId returns the stored Visit reached by traversal and adds nothing. Pet.getVisit(Integer id) traversal accessor mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer id), including its skip-unsaved guard

patterns.description: Post-extraction shape confirmed against the tree at build-pass line 21: loadPetWithVisit now reads 'find owner, find pet, resolveVisit', and resolveVisit is the named home of the in-place invariant (visitId null -> new unsaved Visit added to the pet; visitId present -> the pet's own stored Visit, or IllegalArgumentException). resolveVisit is private, so it takes no Contracts row; the VisitController, Pet, and Visit rows in system-design.md still describe the tree accurately and needed no revision for the extraction.

Owner.getPet(Integer id) is the traversal accessor mirrored by Pet.getVisit(Integer id) (Pet.java:91). The two are independent scopes, which is the substance of the doc-reviewer's finding on system-design.md:80 — see notes.

risks.risk: The aggregate carrier is rebound: both visit handlers (and both PetController form handlers) take the loaded Owner as a save carrier, Spring rebinds request parameters onto the whole aggregate before the handler runs, and the cascading save persists them. The @InitBinder disallow covers id and *.id so identity is safe, but the carrier is not @Valid, so a crafted POST can set and persist fields the form never offers, bypassing Owner's bean-validation constraints.
risks.mitigation: Decided: accept and record, not narrow. Recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-04-aggregate-carrier-rebinding.md, as an invariant in system-design.md § Contracts, and by correcting the Threat Model's 'Unvalidated input reaching persistence' row, which previously overclaimed. No code change this slice — the implementer is NOT asked to touch the controller.

risks.risk: The in-place update is implicit — the POST handler validates and calls save() with no visible mutation, because the mutation happened during binding. A later maintainer may 'fix' it by adding an addVisit call and reintroduce the duplicate.
risks.mitigation: resolveVisit now names the branch, the handler carries a comment stating why it does not re-add, and theVisitCorrectionShouldLeaveThePetsVisitCountUnchanged is the executable guard.

risks.risk: Identifier tampering — a visitId belonging to another pet, or a petId belonging to another owner.
risks.mitigation: Closed by the design rather than by an added check: no VisitRepository and no global lookup by visit id exist, so the only route is owner -> pet -> visit and a foreign id is not found. system-design.md:80 now states this at both traversal levels, covering PRD Visits edge case 3's two clauses.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log, skipped. WHAT I PROCESSED, all from review-feedback line 19 (doc-reviewer) and line 17 (security-reviewer). (1) ADR 30-word cap, docs/adr/2026-08-04-non-goal-visit-correction.md:7,9,26 — all three split at the existing boundaries (comma, colon, em-dash); the stated options, decision, and consequences are unchanged word-for-word otherwise. I re-counted every other sentence in that ADR; none exceeds the cap. (2) system-design.md:80 substantive — FINDING ACCEPTED AND CORRECT. My clause stated the guard only at the owner level, which understates it. Pet.getVisit(visitId) iterates that pet's own visits collection, so a visitId belonging to a different pet under the SAME owner misses by the identical mechanism, with no foreign owner involved. The clause now reads as three sentences: traversal never a global lookup; each level scoped independently, naming the petId-outside-owner's-pets and visitId-outside-pet's-visits cases; and an explicit sentence that a same-owner different-pet visit is refused by the second level alone. That matches PRD Visits edge case 3 clause one and the passing theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitBelongsToAnotherPet. (3) system-design.md:80 length — fixed by the same rewrite; every new sentence is at or under 26 words. (4) system-design.md:97 length — FINDING'S COUNT IS WRONG, FIX APPLIED ANYWAY. The VisitController Purpose cell is 24 words, not 34; the reviewer appears to have counted the whole table row including the source path. I applied the proposed split regardless because the semicolon-joined cell reads as a run-on and the split is a clear improvement, but flagging the miscount so the 34 is not treated as authoritative. THE SECURITY-REVIEWER'S CLARIFY, DECIDED: accept and record, option 1 of the two offered. Reasoning, recorded in full in the new docs/adr/2026-08-04-aggregate-carrier-rebinding.md: security-principles.md § Applying this section is dispositive — a change fails only if it introduces a listed class or leaves the app weaker than the baseline, and this change does neither, since three pre-existing handlers (the visit booking POST and both PetController form POSTs) carry the identical carrier shape and the app is unauthenticated by design. Narrowing only the two visit handlers would harden two of four and leave a reader inferring the other two are deliberate, which teaches something more false than the current uniform shape; narrowing all four is the correct end state but is a codebase-wide change with no requirement behind it and does not belong folded into REQ-VIS-003. NO CODE CHANGE IS REQUESTED OF THE IMPLEMENTER for this finding. The one thing the reviewer found that WAS a genuine defect is the documentation overclaim: the Threat Model's 'Unvalidated input reaching persistence' mitigation implied the entity constraints gate everything reaching persistence when they gate the @Valid form object alone. That row is now marked Partial and states the carrier gap with an ADR back-link. FOR THE PRD OWNER, not actioned here: narrowing every carrier handler to @ModelAttribute(binding = false) is worth a slice of its own, with a requirement behind it. I did not add it to system-design.md § Open Questions from the Survey, since that section is scoped to the bootstrap survey and this was not found there. CONTRACTS ROWS VERIFIED against the post-extraction tree (build-pass line 21): resolveVisit is private and takes no row; the VisitController, Pet, and Visit rows still describe the tree accurately and were changed only for the sentence split. Basis is direct reads of VisitController, PetController, Owner, Pet and a grep for the visit accessors; no IDE oracle is connected in this dispatch, so no search_symbol citation accompanies the claim. Two PRD open questions remain unresolved and non-blocking: whether a past visit should be correctable, and how a correction is reached from the owner's record.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Round-1 clarify finding resolved: docs/adr/2026-08-04-aggregate-carrier-rebinding.md states the gap accurately. Verified each factual claim against source: VisitController.setAllowedFields disallows 'id','*.id' (line 53); both carrier params are @ModelAttribute Owner without @Valid (lines 131, 155); the cascade save is real (owners.save(owner) on the Owner aggregate). The enumeration of four carrier handlers is complete, not merely plausible - a sweep of all @ModelAttribute/@PostMapping/@Valid sites in src/main/java finds exactly four Owner-as-carrier handlers (VisitController:131, VisitController:155, PetController:108, PetController:145) and no fifth instance. OwnerController's two POST handlers bind @Valid Owner as the form object itself, so they are not carriers and are correctly excluded.

Reasoning holds against docs/security-principles.md. The Applying-this-section test asks two questions. (1) Does the change introduce a class in the table? The Mass assignment row's named control is 'every request-bound type explicitly disallows identifier binding; a new controller or binder that omits the disallow list fails' - the controller-wide @InitBinder is present and the change adds no new binder, so the control is met. (2) Does the change leave the application weaker than the baseline? No - the new endpoint carries a shape three pre-existing handlers already carry, under the same disallow list, in an application that is unauthenticated by design per system-design.md Security Context. The Widening-the-exposed-surface row is also satisfied: the change adds two endpoints and states what they expose, in the PRD requirement, the Contracts row, and the ADR. Accept-and-record is a defensible reading of a brief whose own rule is that pre-existing absences are never findings.

The ADR does not launder the residual risk. Its Consequences name the demonstration-propagation concern as deferred rather than closed, and it keeps narrowing-every-carrier-handler as a follow-up slice with a requirement behind it. That is the honest form of this decision: the reason to reject option 1 (partial hardening teaches a reader the untouched handlers are deliberate) is sound, and option 2's codebase-wide scope genuinely exceeds this slice.

Threat Model row 'Unvalidated input reaching persistence' now reads Partial and states the actual coverage boundary - the constraints gate the @Valid form object alone, while the Owner carrier is rebound and saved without revalidation. That is the correction the round-1 finding asked for; the prior wording implied entity constraints gated everything reaching persistence. The ADR back-link resolves, and the matching invariant in system-design.md Contracts states the breadth where a reader meets the pattern.

Traversal guard preserved through the resolveVisit(Pet, Integer, int) extraction. The two authorization levels remain independent and both stayed inside the guarded path: loadPetWithVisit resolves the owner by path ownerId, then owner.getPet(petId) restricts to that owner's own pets and throws when absent; resolveVisit then calls pet.getVisit(visitId) on that already-scoped pet, throwing when the visit is not among that pet's own visits. The extraction moved code, not control flow - no lookup was widened to a global one, no null check was dropped, and the new Pet.getVisit iterates only this.visits with an isNew() skip so an unsaved visit cannot be matched. An IDOR across owners or across sibling pets under one owner remains unreachable.

Both traversal levels are now pinned by tests. theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitBelongsToAnotherPet covers the visit-level scope and the new theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenThePetBelongsToAnotherOwner covers the pet-level scope, each asserting the refusal and that the pet's visit collection is unchanged - so a future refactor that collapses either level fails a test rather than silently opening an IDOR.

Supply chain unchanged since round 1: build.gradle is not in the change set, so no new or upgraded dependency entered this pass and no new CVE surface was introduced. Error messages on the refusal paths carry only the ids from the request path, so the error page renders no value the caller did not already supply.

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: Eight files, one production package (owner) plus its test package and docs; no sensitive paths, no schema, config or dependency change. The one shared surface touched is loadPetWithVisit, whose booking path is byte-for-byte the old behaviour behind a null visitId and stays covered by the existing booking tests.

semantic_surprise.note: The persistence logic holds up on a close read: resolveVisit adds nothing on the correction path, Pet.getVisit scopes to the pet's own saved visits, binding mutates the stored visit in place and the cascade save persists it. The surprise is presentational and invisible in the diff, which touches no template: createOrUpdateVisitForm.html filters Previous Visits on the iterated visit being unsaved, so the correction page lists the visit being corrected inside its own Previous Visits table, and the submit button still renders the addVisit key, 'Add Visit'. Nothing links to the new route either, so the feature ships reachable only by typed URL. All three are recorded as known and out of scope, not fixed.

test_adequacy.note: Eleven tests assert real outcomes on the in-memory aggregate rather than restating the implementation: containsExactly(bookedVisit) would fail if a correction booked a second visit, the date and description assertions would fail if binding never reached the stored visit, and both refusal branches (foreign visitId, foreign petId) assert the untouched collection. They would not catch a dropped owners.save, since the repository is a mock, but that is the suite's pre-existing convention and no test at this level could prove persistence.

reviewer_hedging.note: Round 2 is unanimous approval with empty findings lists, and the round-1 code-quality and test findings were closed by real work the reviewers re-verified by reading the extracted helper and the new refusal test. The hedge is security's: its round-1 clarify described a mass-assignment sink on the new endpoint's @ModelAttribute Owner carrier, which the slice closed by writing an accept-and-record ADR rather than the one-annotation narrowing, and the approving prose calls that 'a defensible reading'. The ADR itself says the demonstration-propagation concern is 'deferred, not closed', and the threat model's unvalidated-input row was downgraded to 'Partial' in the same slice.

scope_deviation.note: The code stays exactly on the requirement's stated surface: two endpoints, one traversal accessor, one behaviour-preserving extraction. The two design revisions were procedural rather than scope fights, one adding the docs paths the autofix audit needed and one writing the Contracts rows after the code landed, and the NG-5 narrowing was an authorized product-owner decision recorded before the requirement, with consultations and build retries both at zero.

rationale: Code and tests are sound; the residuals want a human's endorsement, not a re-review. The untouched form template lists the visit under correction as a previous visit and still reads 'Add Visit', and nothing links to the route. The new endpoint inherits an aggregate-carrier rebinding sink the slice accepted rather than narrowed. Read both ADRs and the downgraded threat-model row.
